FDA Approval and Regulation of Companion Diagnostics
We expect that our product candidates may require use of a diagnostic to identify appropriate patient populations for our products. These diagnostics, often referred to as companion diagnostics, are medical devices, often in vitro devices, which provide information that is essential for the safe and effective use of a corresponding drug. In the United States, the FDCA and its implementing regulations, and other federal and state statutes and regulations govern, among other things, medical device design and development, preclinical and clinical testing, premarket clearance or approval, registration and listing, manufacturing, labeling, storage, advertising and promotion, sales and distribution, export and import and post-market surveillance. Unless an exemption applies, diagnostic tests require marketing clearance or approval from the FDA prior to commercial distribution. The two primary types of FDA marketing authorization applicable to a medical device are premarket notification, also called 510(k) clearance, and premarket approval, or PMA approval. We expect that any companion diagnostic developed for our product candidates will utilize the PMA pathway.
The PMA process, including the gathering of clinical and preclinical data and the submission to and review by the FDA, can take several years or longer. It involves a rigorous premarket review during which the applicant must prepare and provide the FDA with reasonable assurance of the device’s safety and effectiveness and information about the device and its components regarding, among other things, device design, manufacturing and labeling. PMA applications are subject to an application fee. In addition, PMAs for certain devices must generally include the results from extensive preclinical and adequate and well-controlled clinical trials to establish the safety and effectiveness of the device for each indication for which FDA approval is sought. In particular, for a diagnostic, a PMA application typically requires data regarding analytical and clinical validation studies. As part of the PMA review, the FDA will typically inspect the manufacturer’s facilities for compliance with the Quality System
34

Regulation, or QSR, which imposes elaborate testing, control, documentation and other quality assurance requirements.
PMA approval is not guaranteed, and the FDA may ultimately respond to a PMA submission with a not approvable determination based on deficiencies in the application and require additional clinical trial or other data that may be expensive and time-consuming to generate and that can substantially delay approval. If the FDA’s evaluation of the PMA application is favorable, the FDA typically issues an approvable letter requiring the applicant’s agreement to specific conditions, such as changes in labeling, or specific additional information, such as submission of final labeling, in order to secure final approval of the PMA. If the FDA’s evaluation of the PMA or manufacturing facilities is not favorable, the FDA will deny approval of the PMA or issue a not approvable letter. A not approvable letter will outline the deficiencies in the application and, where practical, will identify what is necessary to make the PMA approvable. The FDA may also determine that additional clinical trials are necessary, in which case the PMA approval may be delayed for several months or years while the trials are conducted and then the data submitted in an amendment to the PMA. If the FDA concludes that the applicable criteria have been met, the FDA will issue a PMA for the approved indications, which can be more limited than those originally sought by the applicant. The PMA can include post-approval conditions that the FDA believes necessary to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the device, including, among other things, restrictions on labeling, promotion, sale and distribution. Once granted, PMA approval may be withdrawn by the FDA if compliance with post approval requirements, conditions of approval or other regulatory standards are not maintained, or problems are identified following initial marketing.

In August 2014, the FDA issued final guidance clarifying the requirements that will apply to approval of therapeutic products and in vitro companion diagnostics. According to the guidance, if FDA determines that a companion diagnostic device is essential to the safe and effective use of a novel therapeutic product or indication, FDA generally will not approve the therapeutic product or new therapeutic product indication if the companion diagnostic device is not approved or cleared for that indication at the same time. The review of in vitro companion diagnostics in conjunction with the review of our therapeutic treatments for cancer will, therefore, likely involve coordination of review by the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research and the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health Office of In Vitro Diagnostics. The guidance also explains that a companion diagnostic device used to make treatment decisions in clinical trials of a drug generally will be considered an investigational device, unless it is employed for an intended use for which the device is already approved or cleared. If used to make critical treatment decisions, such as patient selection, the diagnostic device generally will be considered a significant risk device under the FDA’s Investigational Device Exemption, or IDE, regulations. Thus, the sponsor of the diagnostic device will be required to comply with the IDE regulations. According to the guidance, if a diagnostic device and a drug are to be studied together to support their respective approvals, both products can be studied in the same investigational study, if the study meets both the requirements of the IDE regulations and the IND regulations. The guidance provides that depending on the details of the study plan and subjects, a sponsor may seek to submit an IND alone, or both an IND and an IDE. After a device is placed on the market, it remains subject to significant regulatory requirements. Medical devices may be marketed only for the uses and indications for which they are cleared or approved. Device manufacturers must also establish registration and device listings with the FDA. A medical device manufacturer’s manufacturing processes and those of its suppliers are required to comply with the applicable portions of the QSR, which cover the methods and documentation of the design, testing, production, processes, controls, quality assurance, labeling, packaging and shipping of medical devices. Domestic facility records and manufacturing processes are subject to periodic unscheduled inspections by the FDA. The FDA also may inspect foreign facilities that export products to the United States.

DEPARTMENT OF REVENUE  SERVICES
AGENCY DESCRIPTION
___________________________________________________________________________________________
The Department of Revenue Services (DRS) is statutorily responsible for administering and enforcing state tax laws and collecting state tax revenues  
while safeguarding and protecting Connecticut taxpayer rights, privacy and property. The agency is responsible for ensuring taxpayer compliance with  
tax  laws  and,  when  necessary,  initiating  actions  to  collect  unpaid  taxes  and  applying  enforcement  measures.  DRS  is  responsible  for  exercising  its  
authority fairly and impartially for both  the State and  the taxpayer.
The agency administers five programs designed to accomplish its major business objectives: to collect what is due, increase taxpayer compliance,  
protect taxpayer  information, treat taxpayers fairly and consistently, and reduce the cost of  performance.

Upon completion of this offering, we will become a public company in the United States subject to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 will require that we include a report of management on our internal control over financial reporting in our annual report on Form 20-F beginning with our annual report for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2025. In addition, once we cease to be an “emerging growth company,” as such term is defined in the JOBS Act, our independent registered public accounting firm must attest to and report on the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting. Our management may conclude that our internal control over financial reporting is not effective. Moreover, even if our management concludes that our internal control over financial reporting is effective, our independent registered public accounting firm, after conducting its own independent testing, may issue a report that is qualified if it is not satisfied with our internal controls or the level at which our controls are documented, designed, operated, or reviewed, or if it interprets the relevant requirements differently from us. In addition, after we become a public company, our reporting obligations may place a significant strain on our management, operational, and financial resources and systems for the foreseeable future. We may be unable to complete our evaluation testing and any required remediation in a timely manner.
Our management has broad discretion to determine how to use the funds raised in the offering and may use them in ways that may not enhance our results of operations or the price of our Ordinary Shares.
We anticipate that we will use the net proceeds from this offering to commercialize nutraceutical formulations in key markets, to expand our manufacturing capacity and scale regulatory-compliant production, to find clinical development of our lead candidate, SKF7®, to support preclinical and IND-enabling studies for KPH1™ and MKS5®, as well as for working capital and general corporate purposes. Our management will have significant discretion as to the use of the net proceeds to us from this offering and could spend the proceeds in ways that do not improve our results of operations or enhance the market price of our Ordinary Shares. Pending their use, we may invest the net proceeds from this offering in a manner that does not produce income or that loses value.
texts.107:
We are an “emerging growth company” within the meaning of the Securities Act, and if we take advantage of certain exemptions from disclosure requirements available to emerging growth companies, this will make it more difficult to compare our performance with other public companies.
We are an “emerging growth company” within the meaning of the Securities Act, as modified by the JOBS Act. Section 102(b)(1) of the JOBS Act exempts emerging growth companies from being required to comply with new or revised financial accounting standards until private companies (that is, those that have not had a Securities Act registration statement declared effective or do not have a class of securities registered under the Exchange Act) are required to comply with the new or revised financial accounting standards. The JOBS Act provides that a company can elect to opt out of the extended transition period and comply with the requirements that apply to non-emerging growth companies but any such an election to opt out is irrevocable. We have elected not to opt out of such extended transition period, which means that when a standard is issued or revised and it has different application dates for public or private companies, we, as an emerging growth company, can adopt the new or revised standard at the time private companies adopt the new or revised standard. This will make comparison of our financial statements with another public company which is neither an emerging growth company nor an emerging growth company which has opted out of using the extended transition period difficult or impossible because of the potential differences in accounting standards used.
53
Because we are an “emerging growth company,” we may not be subject to requirements that other public companies are subject to, which could affect investor confidence in us and our Ordinary Shares.
texts.108:
For as long as we remain an “emerging growth company,” as defined in the JOBS Act, we will elect to take advantage of certain exemptions from various reporting requirements that are applicable to other public companies that are not “emerging growth companies,” including not being required to comply with the auditor attestation requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, reduced disclosure obligations regarding executive compensation in our periodic reports and proxy statements, and exemptions from the requirements of shareholder approval of any golden parachute payments not previously approved. Because of these lessened regulatory requirements, our shareholders would be left without information or rights available to shareholders of more mature companies. If some investors find our Ordinary Shares less attractive as a result, there may be a less active trading market for our Ordinary Shares and our share price may be more volatile. See “Implications of Our Being an ‘Emerging Growth Company.’”
Future sales of our securities by existing shareholders could depress the market price of our Ordinary Shares.
25,555,160 of our Ordinary Shares are issued and outstanding as of the date of this prospectus. A substantial percentage of our Ordinary Shares outstanding prior to this offering are subject to the six (6) month contractual lockup. See “Underwriting”. The holders of these Ordinary Shares and our other Ordinary Shares outstanding prior to this offering may be able to sell their Ordinary Shares under Rule 144 after such contractual lock-up and other legal restrictions on resale lapse. See “Shares Eligible for Future Sale” below. Because these shareholders have paid a lower price per Ordinary Share than participants in this offering, when they are able to sell their pre-IPO shares, they may be more willing to accept a lower sales price than the IPO price, which could impact the future trading price of our Ordinary Shares, to the detriment of participants in this offering.
Our shareholders may be held liable for claims by third parties against us to the extent of distributions received by them upon a subsequent liquidation of the company.
texts.109:
If Medikra is placed into liquidation within 6 years following the payment of a distribution, there is a risk that the payment would be voidable by a liquidator if the liquidator can establish that it was made with the intent to defraud creditors (regardless of whether Medikra was solvent at the time of making the distribution). In addition, if Medikra is placed into liquidation at any time, and it appears that the distribution was paid with intention to defraud creditors, then there is a risk that any persons who were knowingly parties to such fraud may be personally liable to contribute to the company’s assets (regardless of whether Medikra was solvent at the time of paying the dividend).
We may not have sufficient funds to satisfy indemnification claims of our directors and officers.
We have agreed to indemnify our officers and directors to the fullest extent permitted by law, including for any liability incurred in their capacities as such, except through their own actual fraud, willful default or dishonesty. Our obligation to indemnify our officers and directors may discourage shareholders from bringing a lawsuit against our officers or directors for breach of their fiduciary duty. These provisions also may have the effect of reducing the likelihood of derivative litigation against our officers and directors, even though such an action, if successful, might otherwise benefit us and our shareholders. Furthermore, a shareholder’s investment may be adversely affected to the extent we pay the costs of settlement and damage awards against our officers and directors pursuant to these indemnification provisions.
Cayman Islands economic substance requirements may have an effect on our business and operations.
Pursuant to the International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Act (Revised) (the “ES Act”) together with the Guidance Notes published by the Cayman Islands Tax Information Authority from time to time, if a company is considered to be a “relevant entity” and is conducting one or more of the nine “relevant activities” then that company will be required to satisfy the economic substance test and comply with the economic substance requirements in relation to the relevant activity as set out in the ES Act. All companies whether a relevant entity or not are required to file an annual report in the Cayman Islands with the Registrar of Companies in the Cayman Islands confirming whether or not it is carrying on any relevant activities.

## How the SEC Assigns a CIK Number
### EDGAR CIK login, password and confirmation codes
People searching for "EDGAR CIK login" or "EDGAR CIK password" are usually looking for filer credentials, not for public data. It is worth being precise about the difference, because the CIK itself is public and the credentials are not:
*   **CIK** - public. Printed on filings, published in bulk files, safe to share.  
*   **Passphrase / password** - private. Used to authenticate a filing session.  
*   **CCC (CIK Confirmation Code)** - private. Pairs with the CIK to authorize a submission.  
*   **Access codes for agents** - private. Let a filing agent transmit on a client's behalf.
Nobody can file on your behalf using only your CIK. If a service asks you for a CCC or passphrase, treat that request with the same care you would a banking credential. EDGARScout never asks for and never handles filer credentials.

## How the SEC Assigns a CIK Number
### What CIK ranges tell you about a filer
Sequence position is a rough vintage signal, not a rule. Five- and six-digit CIKs generally belong to registrants that existed when the index was first populated - International Business Machines Corp is `0000051143` and Johnson & Johnson is `0000200406`. Seven-digit CIKs beginning with 1 were largely issued from the late 1990s onward, and CIKs beginning with 2 are recent. Sweetgreen, Inc. at `0001477815` and CAVA GROUP, INC. at `0001639438` reflect their much later arrival, while Situational Awareness LP at `0002045724` is newer still.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
A **reverse CIK lookup** answers the question "which company does this number belong to?" and it takes one request. Given any CIK, pad it to 10 digits and fetch the submissions JSON; the response contains the registrant's current name, former names, state of incorporation, business address, SIC code and full filing history. This is the authoritative answer - it comes from the SEC, not from a third-party mirror.
You Have the Number. Who Is It?

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### How to look up any company by CIK number
Three routes work, in decreasing order of detail:
1.   **Submissions API**-`https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000084839.json` returns name, tickers, addresses, state of incorporation and every filing.  
2.   **EDGAR company viewer**-`https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?cik=84839` renders the same record as a page.  
3.   **Classic browse-edgar**-`https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000084839&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40` gives the filing table with a header block showing state and SIC.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Which JSON fields answer "company name and state"?
The searches that ask for a CIK plus "company name state" are really asking for four fields. Read them from the submissions document rather than scraping HTML:
*   `name` - the current registered name as EDGAR holds it.  
*   `formerNames[]` - every prior name with the dates it was in effect.  
*   `stateOfIncorporation` - the legal domicile, often DE.  
*   `addresses.business.stateOrCountry` - the operating location, frequently different from the domicile.  
*   `sic` and `sicDescription` - the industry classification, explained on our SIC code lookup page.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Domicile is not location
Expect the two state fields to disagree. Rollins Inc is incorporated in Delaware but operates from Georgia. Global Medical Response, Inc. is a Delaware entity with a Colorado business address. If a report needs "where the company is," decide explicitly which of the two you mean before you build the column.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Confirming you have the right entity
A reverse lookup that returns a plausible-looking name is not the same as a confirmed match. Before you rely on it, check three things: that the filing history contains the forms you would expect for the entity type, that the business address is consistent with what you know about the company, and that the ticker array either matches your expectation or is legitimately empty. If any of the three surprises you, you may be looking at a subsidiary, a similarly named registrant, or a dormant shell. Recording the entity name next to every CIK you store makes this kind of mismatch visible later instead of silently propagating through a dataset.

## Worked CIK Examples From Real EDGAR Records
The fastest way to internalize **CIK codes** is to look at real ones. Every value in the tables below was read directly from `data.sec.gov/submissions/` rather than reproduced from memory, and each can be verified in one request. Note how often the registered name differs from the brand you would search for.

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
**`cik-lookup-data.txt` is the full EDGAR CIK list** - every filer name the SEC has ever indexed, mapped to a CIK, in one plain-text file at `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt`. Where the ticker map covers listed companies only, this file covers individuals, funds, trusts, agents, dissolved registrants and historical names, which makes it the right source for an **EDGAR CIK database download**.

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
### Format and parsing
Each line is an uppercase filer name, then a colon, then the padded CIK, then a trailing colon. Names may themselves contain colons and commas, so split from the right, never from the left.
```  
import urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request(  
    "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt",  
    headers={"User-Agent": "YourCompany you@example.com"})

index = {}  
for raw in urllib.request.urlopen(req):  
    line = raw.decode("latin-1").strip().rstrip(":")  
    if not line:  
        continue  
    name, _, cik = line.rpartition(":")  
    if cik.isdigit():  
        index.setdefault(name, cik)

print(len(index), "names indexed")  
```

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
### Practical notes before you rely on it
*   The file is large - stream it rather than reading it into memory as one string.  
*   Encoding is not clean UTF-8; decode with a permissive codec such as latin-1.  
*   Names are uppercase, so normalize your query the same way.  
*   One CIK can appear under several names, including former names.  
*   Refresh periodically; new registrants are added continuously.

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
### When to use this instead of the tool above
Use the interactive lookup for one-off questions about listed companies. Use the bulk file when you need offline resolution, when you are matching thousands of names at once, or when your targets include non-listed entities such as private issuers and Section 16 individuals that the ticker map simply does not contain.

## EDGAR CIK Database Download Options Compared
**The SEC publishes several free bulk files that contain CIKs**, each with a different scope and shape. Choosing the right one first saves a great deal of parsing work later, so compare coverage before you write a downloader.

## EDGAR CIK Database Download Options Compared
### Which bulk file should you download?
Which File Should You Download?
| Resource | Scope | Format | Best for |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| `company_tickers.json` | Listed registrants with tickers | JSON | Ticker to CIK resolution |  
| `company_tickers_exchange.json` | Listed registrants plus venue | JSON | Exchange-aware mapping |  
| `cik-lookup-data.txt` | All filer names ever indexed | Delimited text | Offline name to CIK matching |  
| Quarterly full index files | Every filing in a quarter | Text and JSON idx | Rebuilding a filing archive |  
| Daily index files | Every filing on one day | Text and JSON idx | Incremental daily updates |  
| Financial statement data sets | XBRL numeric data by quarter | Zipped TSV | Cross-company fundamentals |  
| Submissions bulk archive | Every filer's submissions JSON | Large ZIP | Full local mirror of filing metadata |

## EDGAR CIK Database Download Options Compared
### Index files are CIK-keyed too
Every quarterly and daily index row includes the CIK, the company name, the form type, the filing date and the document path. That makes the index files a second route to a name-to-CIK table, and the only convenient route to "every filer that submitted a given form in a given quarter."

## EDGAR CIK Database Download Options Compared
### Etiquette when downloading in bulk
*   Send a descriptive User-Agent containing a real contact address.  
*   Stay within the published fair-access limit of about 10 requests per second.  
*   Prefer one bulk file over thousands of individual requests.  
*   Cache aggressively and honor HTTP caching headers.  
*   Retry with backoff rather than hammering after an error.
The same etiquette applies to every endpoint discussed in our EDGAR API guide; sustained abuse gets IP addresses throttled.

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
**The submissions endpoint turns a CIK into a complete filing history** in one request: `https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json`, with the CIK padded to ten digits. It is the workhorse of EDGAR automation and returns both the entity's descriptive record and its recent filings as parallel arrays.

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### What the response contains
*   `cik`, `name`, `tickers`, `exchanges`, `entityType`.  
*   `sic`, `sicDescription`, `stateOfIncorporation`, `addresses`.  
*   `formerNames` with effective date ranges.  
*   `filings.recent` - parallel arrays of accession numbers, form types, filing dates and document names.  
*   `filings.files` - references to older pages of history for prolific filers.

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### A runnable example
```  
import json, urllib.request

def submissions(cik):  
    url = f"https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{str(cik).zfill(10)}.json"  
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={  
        "User-Agent": "YourCompany you@example.com"})  
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))

d = submissions(84839)  
print(d["name"], d["stateOfIncorporation"], d["addresses"]["business"]["stateOrCountry"])

rec = d["filings"]["recent"]  
for form, date, acc in list(zip(rec["form"], rec["filingDate"], rec["accessionNumber"]))[:5]:  
    print(form, date, acc)  
```

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### Building a document URL from the result
Filing documents live under `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accession-no-dashes}/{document}`. Note the inconsistency that trips people up: the path uses the _unpadded_ CIK while the JSON you just fetched used the padded one. Strip the dashes from the accession number for the folder name and keep them for display.

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### Paging through a long filing history
The `filings.recent` block holds only the most recent tranche of submissions. Prolific filers - large banks, fund complexes, and any issuer with decades of ownership forms - overflow it, and the remainder is referenced in `filings.files` as additional JSON documents under the same submissions path. If you need a complete history you must fetch those extra files and concatenate them; skipping this step produces a truncated record that looks complete. A useful sanity check is to compare the earliest filing date you retrieved against the entity's known vintage, since a company with a five-digit CIK showing only three years of history is a clear sign that paging was missed.

## Using a CIK in EDGAR Full-Text Search
**Full-text search accepts a CIK as a filter**, which lets you search words inside one company's filings rather than across all of EDGAR. The system indexes filing documents from 2001 onward, so it complements - rather than replaces - the metadata search you get from the submissions API.
One Number Opens Five Doors

## Using a CIK in EDGAR Full-Text Search
### The query endpoint
The public interface is at `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=`, and the browser UI at `https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/` is built on it. Combine a quoted phrase with an entity restriction and, optionally, form and date filters. Our full-text search tool exposes the same filters without the URL assembly.

## Why Do You Need a CIK Number?
### For Analysts & Researchers
*   **Historical research** - track filings through renamings/mergers  
*   **Data normalization** - link SEC data to other databases  
*   **Filing tracking** - monitor a specific entity over time  
*   **Compliance** - verify which entity actually files with SEC  
*   **Cross-references** - match SEC data to CRSP or Compustat

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What is a CIK number?
A CIK (Central Index Key) is the unique identifier the SEC assigns to every entity that files with EDGAR. It is written as up to 10 digits, zero-padded on the left in its canonical form. Apple Inc.'s CIK is 0000320193 and MICROSOFT CORP's is 0000789019. A CIK never changes, even when the company renames itself or changes its ticker symbol.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What does CIK stand for in EDGAR?
CIK stands for Central Index Key. It is the number the SEC's systems use to identify corporations and individuals who have filed disclosure documents with the Commission. The same number is used across every SEC program area, so one CIK covers annual reports, ownership forms and institutional holdings reports alike.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Is an EDGAR CIK always 10 digits?
The canonical form is 10 digits with leading zeros, but the underlying number can be shorter. Apple's CIK is 320193 as an integer and 0000320193 when padded. Path-based endpoints such as data.sec.gov/submissions/ require the padded form, while query-string parameters like browse-edgar's CIK= accept either.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I look up a company by CIK number?
Pad the number to 10 digits and open https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000084839.json, substituting your CIK. The response gives the registrant's current name, former names, state of incorporation, business address, SIC code and complete filing history. For a rendered page instead, open https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?cik=84839.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I find a company's CIK from its ticker?
Use the lookup tool at the top of this page, which searches the SEC's official company_tickers.json file. For automated work, download that file once from https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json, build a ticker-to-CIK dictionary in memory, and resolve your whole list locally rather than issuing one request per ticker.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I get a CIK number for my own company?
A CIK is issued automatically when an entity applies for EDGAR filing access through the SEC's filer-management process; you cannot request a specific number. The application also produces the private credentials used to transmit filings. Under EDGAR Next, access is managed through individual account credentials and authorized users, but the CIK itself is unchanged.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What is the difference between a CIK and a CIK confirmation code?
The CIK is public - it is printed on filings and published in SEC bulk files. The CIK Confirmation Code (CCC) is a private credential that pairs with the CIK to authorize a submission, as is the filer passphrase. Sharing a CIK is harmless; sharing a CCC or passphrase is not. EDGARScout never asks for filer credentials.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Why does one company have several CIK numbers?
Because EDGAR assigns CIKs to legal filing entities, not to brands. A group can have separate CIKs for the listed parent, financing subsidiaries and co-registrants, securitization trusts, registered fund trusts, and the advisory entity that files 13F reports. Choose the CIK by the form you need rather than by the most familiar name.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Does a CIK change when a company changes its name or ticker?
No. NAUTILUS, INC. became BOWFLEX INC. and kept CIK 0001078207; Facebook Inc became Meta Platforms, Inc. under 0001326801. EDGAR updates the name field and records the prior name in the formerNames array while the CIK stays fixed. A genuinely new legal registrant created by a merger does receive its own new CIK.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Can I look up a fund's CIK number?
Yes. Registered funds, ETFs, closed-end funds and the managers that file 13F reports all have CIKs. Search the registered legal name rather than the marketing name, and expect a layered structure: a registrant CIK for the trust, with S000 series identifiers and C000 class identifiers underneath it for individual funds and share classes.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Do individual people have CIK numbers?
Yes. Officers, directors and large shareholders who file Section 16 ownership forms have their own CIKs - Elon Musk's is 0001494730. EDGAR stores personal names surname-first with no comma, as "Musk Elon", so search the surname alone. The most reliable route is to open any Form 4 for the issuer and read the reporting person's CIK from the header.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Where can I download the full EDGAR CIK list?
The SEC publishes cik-lookup-data.txt at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt, containing every filer name ever indexed with its padded CIK. Lines are name, colon, CIK, colon - split from the right because names can contain colons. For listed companies only, company_tickers.json is smaller and easier to work with.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Why does my CIK search return multiple companies?
EDGAR matches your text against every registrant name, and many names overlap - subsidiaries, funds, dissolved shells and unrelated companies can all contain the same word. Use the state column and SIC description to discriminate, then open the candidate and confirm its filing history contains the forms you would expect from the entity you want.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What happens to a CIK when a company is delisted or acquired?
Nothing is deleted. The CIK and the full filing archive remain permanently retrievable, and the history simply stops - often shortly after a Form 25 or Form 15. Because the current ticker map contains only survivors, any historical study must enumerate these dormant CIKs as well, or it will suffer from survivorship bias.
**Disclaimer:** Data sourced from SEC EDGAR public filings via the official EDGAR API (data.sec.gov). This tool is for informational purposes only and is **not financial or investment advice**. Always verify data directly on SEC.gov.

1.   **Submissions API**-`https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000084839.json` returns name, tickers, addresses, state of incorporation and every filing.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Which JSON fields answer "company name and state"?
The searches that ask for a CIK plus "company name state" are really asking for four fields. Read them from the submissions document rather than scraping HTML:
*   `name` - the current registered name as EDGAR holds it.  
*   `formerNames[]` - every prior name with the dates it was in effect.  
*   `stateOfIncorporation` - the legal domicile, often DE.  
*   `addresses.business.stateOrCountry` - the operating location, frequently different from the domicile.  
*   `sic` and `sicDescription` - the industry classification, explained on our SIC code lookup page.
texts.24:
## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Domicile is not location
Expect the two state fields to disagree. Rollins Inc is incorporated in Delaware but operates from Georgia. Global Medical Response, Inc. is a Delaware entity with a Colorado business address. If a report needs "where the company is," decide explicitly which of the two you mean before you build the column.
texts.25:
## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Confirming you have the right entity
A reverse lookup that returns a plausible-looking name is not the same as a confirmed match. Before you rely on it, check three things: that the filing history contains the forms you would expect for the entity type, that the business address is consistent with what you know about the company, and that the ticker array either matches your expectation or is legitimately empty. If any of the three surprises you, you may be looking at a subsidiary, a similarly named registrant, or a dormant shell. Recording the entity name next to every CIK you store makes this kind of mismatch visible later instead of silently propagating through a dataset.

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
**`cik-lookup-data.txt` is the full EDGAR CIK list** - every filer name the SEC has ever indexed, mapped to a CIK, in one plain-text file at `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt`. texts.65:
## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
### Format and parsing
Each line is an uppercase filer name, then a colon, then the padded CIK, then a trailing colon. Names may themselves contain colons and commas, so split from the right, never from the left.
```  
import urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request(  
    "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt",  
    headers={"User-Agent": "YourCompany you@example.com"})

index = {}  
for raw in urllib.request.urlopen(req):  
    line = raw.decode("latin-1").strip().rstrip(":")  
    if not line:  
        continue  
    name, _, cik = line.rpartition(":")  
    if cik.isdigit():  
        index.setdefault(name, cik)

print(len(index), "names indexed")  
```
texts.66:
## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
### Practical notes before you rely on it
*   The file is large - stream it rather than reading it into memory as one string.  
*   Encoding is not clean UTF-8; decode with a permissive codec such as latin-1.  
*   Names are uppercase, so normalize your query the same way.  
*   One CIK can appear under several names, including former names.  
*   Refresh periodically; new registrants are added continuously.

*   Send a descriptive User-Agent containing a real contact address.

texts.72:
## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
**The submissions endpoint turns a CIK into a complete filing history** in one request: `https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json`, with the CIK padded to ten digits. It is the workhorse of EDGAR automation and returns both the entity's descriptive record and its recent filings as parallel arrays.
texts.73:
## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### What the response contains
*   `cik`, `name`, `tickers`, `exchanges`, `entityType`.  
*   `sic`, `sicDescription`, `stateOfIncorporation`, `addresses`.  
*   `formerNames` with effective date ranges.  
*   `filings.recent` - parallel arrays of accession numbers, form types, filing dates and document names.  
*   `filings.files` - references to older pages of history for prolific filers.
texts.74:
## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### A runnable example
```  
import json, urllib.request

def submissions(cik):  
    url = f"https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{str(cik).zfill(10)}.json"  
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={  
        "User-Agent": "YourCompany you@example.com"})  
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))

d = submissions(84839)  
print(d["name"], d["stateOfIncorporation"], d["addresses"]["business"]["stateOrCountry"])

rec = d["filings"]["recent"]  
for form, date, acc in list(zip(rec["form"], rec["filingDate"], rec["accessionNumber"]))[:5]:  
    print(form, date, acc)  
```
texts.75:
## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### Building a document URL from the result
Filing documents live under `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accession-no-dashes}/{document}`. Note the inconsistency that trips people up: the path uses the _unpadded_ CIK while the JSON you just fetched used the padded one. Strip the dashes from the accession number for the folder name and keep them for display.
texts.76:
## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### Paging through a long filing history
The `filings.recent` block holds only the most recent tranche of submissions. Prolific filers - large banks, fund complexes, and any issuer with decades of ownership forms - overflow it, and the remainder is referenced in `filings.files` as additional JSON documents under the same submissions path. If you need a complete history you must fetch those extra files and concatenate them; skipping this step produces a truncated record that looks complete. A useful sanity check is to compare the earliest filing date you retrieved against the entity's known vintage, since a company with a five-digit CIK showing only three years of history is a clear sign that paging was missed.
texts.77:
## Using a CIK in EDGAR Full-Text Search
**Full-text search accepts a CIK as a filter**, which lets you search words inside one company's filings rather than across all of EDGAR. The system indexes filing documents from 2001 onward, so it complements - rather than replaces - the metadata search you get from the submissions API.

texts.139:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What is a CIK number?
A CIK (Central Index Key) is the unique identifier the SEC assigns to every entity that files with EDGAR. It is written as up to 10 digits, zero-padded on the left in its canonical form. Apple Inc.'s CIK is 0000320193 and MICROSOFT CORP's is 0000789019. A CIK never changes, even when the company renames itself or changes its ticker symbol.
texts.140:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What does CIK stand for in EDGAR?
CIK stands for Central Index Key. It is the number the SEC's systems use to identify corporations and individuals who have filed disclosure documents with the Commission. The same number is used across every SEC program area, so one CIK covers annual reports, ownership forms and institutional holdings reports alike.
texts.141:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Is an EDGAR CIK always 10 digits?
The canonical form is 10 digits with leading zeros, but the underlying number can be shorter. Apple's CIK is 320193 as an integer and 0000320193 when padded. Path-based endpoints such as data.sec.gov/submissions/ require the padded form, while query-string parameters like browse-edgar's CIK= accept either.
texts.142:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I look up a company by CIK number?
Pad the number to 10 digits and open https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000084839.json, substituting your CIK. The response gives the registrant's current name, former names, state of incorporation, business address, SIC code and complete filing history. For a rendered page instead, open https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?cik=84839.
texts.143:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I find a company's CIK from its ticker?
Use the lookup tool at the top of this page, which searches the SEC's official company_tickers.json file. For automated work, download that file once from https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json, build a ticker-to-CIK dictionary in memory, and resolve your whole list locally rather than issuing one request per ticker.
texts.144:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I get a CIK number for my own company?
A CIK is issued automatically when an entity applies for EDGAR filing access through the SEC's filer-management process; you cannot request a specific number. The application also produces the private credentials used to transmit filings. Under EDGAR Next, access is managed through individual account credentials and authorized users, but the CIK itself is unchanged.
texts.145:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What is the difference between a CIK and a CIK confirmation code?
The CIK is public - it is printed on filings and published in SEC bulk files. The CIK Confirmation Code (CCC) is a private credential that pairs with the CIK to authorize a submission, as is the filer passphrase. Sharing a CIK is harmless; sharing a CCC or passphrase is not. EDGARScout never asks for filer credentials.
texts.146:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Why does one company have several CIK numbers?
Because EDGAR assigns CIKs to legal filing entities, not to brands. A group can have separate CIKs for the listed parent, financing subsidiaries and co-registrants, securitization trusts, registered fund trusts, and the advisory entity that files 13F reports. Choose the CIK by the form you need rather than by the most familiar name.
texts.147:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Does a CIK change when a company changes its name or ticker?
No. NAUTILUS, INC. became BOWFLEX INC. and kept CIK 0001078207; Facebook Inc became Meta Platforms, Inc. under 0001326801. EDGAR updates the name field and records the prior name in the formerNames array while the CIK stays fixed. A genuinely new legal registrant created by a merger does receive its own new CIK.
texts.148:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Can I look up a fund's CIK number?
Yes. Registered funds, ETFs, closed-end funds and the managers that file 13F reports all have CIKs. Search the registered legal name rather than the marketing name, and expect a layered structure: a registrant CIK for the trust, with S000 series identifiers and C000 class identifiers underneath it for individual funds and share classes.
texts.149:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Do individual people have CIK numbers?
Yes. Officers, directors and large shareholders who file Section 16 ownership forms have their own CIKs - Elon Musk's is 0001494730. EDGAR stores personal names surname-first with no comma, as "Musk Elon", so search the surname alone. The most reliable route is to open any Form 4 for the issuer and read the reporting person's CIK from the header.
texts.150:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Where can I download the full EDGAR CIK list?
The SEC publishes cik-lookup-data.txt at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt, containing every filer name ever indexed with its padded CIK. Lines are name, colon, CIK, colon - split from the right because names can contain colons. For listed companies only, company_tickers.json is smaller and easier to work with.
texts.151:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Why does my CIK search return multiple companies?
EDGAR matches your text against every registrant name, and many names overlap - subsidiaries, funds, dissolved shells and unrelated companies can all contain the same word. Use the state column and SIC description to discriminate, then open the candidate and confirm its filing history contains the forms you would expect from the entity you want.
texts.152:
## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What happens to a CIK when a company is delisted or acquired?
Nothing is deleted. The CIK and the full filing archive remain permanently retrievable, and the history simply stops - often shortly after a Form 25 or Form 15. Because the current ticker map contains only survivors, any historical study must enumerate these dormant CIKs as well, or it will suffer from survivorship bias.

## How the SEC Assigns a CIK Number
### EDGAR CIK login, password and confirmation codes
People searching for "EDGAR CIK login" or "EDGAR CIK password" are usually looking for filer credentials, not for public data. It is worth being precise about the difference, because the CIK itself is public and the credentials are not:
*   **CIK** - public. Printed on filings, published in bulk files, safe to share.  
*   **Passphrase / password** - private. Used to authenticate a filing session.  
*   **CCC (CIK Confirmation Code)** - private. Pairs with the CIK to authorize a submission.  
*   **Access codes for agents** - private. Let a filing agent transmit on a client's behalf.
Nobody can file on your behalf using only your CIK. If a service asks you for a CCC or passphrase, treat that request with the same care you would a banking credential. EDGARScout never asks for and never handles filer credentials.

## How the SEC Assigns a CIK Number
### What CIK ranges tell you about a filer
Sequence position is a rough vintage signal, not a rule. Five- and six-digit CIKs generally belong to registrants that existed when the index was first populated - International Business Machines Corp is `0000051143` and Johnson & Johnson is `0000200406`. Seven-digit CIKs beginning with 1 were largely issued from the late 1990s onward, and CIKs beginning with 2 are recent. Sweetgreen, Inc. at `0001477815` and CAVA GROUP, INC. at `0001639438` reflect their much later arrival, while Situational Awareness LP at `0002045724` is newer still.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
A **reverse CIK lookup** answers the question "which company does this number belong to?" and it takes one request. Given any CIK, pad it to 10 digits and fetch the submissions JSON; the response contains the registrant's current name, former names, state of incorporation, business address, SIC code and full filing history. This is the authoritative answer - it comes from the SEC, not from a third-party mirror.
You Have the Number. Who Is It?

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### How to look up any company by CIK number
Three routes work, in decreasing order of detail:
1.   **Submissions API**-`https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000084839.json` returns name, tickers, addresses, state of incorporation and every filing.  
2.   **EDGAR company viewer**-`https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?cik=84839` renders the same record as a page.  
3.   **Classic browse-edgar**-`https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000084839&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40` gives the filing table with a header block showing state and SIC.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Which JSON fields answer "company name and state"?
The searches that ask for a CIK plus "company name state" are really asking for four fields. Read them from the submissions document rather than scraping HTML:
*   `name` - the current registered name as EDGAR holds it.  
*   `formerNames[]` - every prior name with the dates it was in effect.  
*   `stateOfIncorporation` - the legal domicile, often DE.  
*   `addresses.business.stateOrCountry` - the operating location, frequently different from the domicile.  
*   `sic` and `sicDescription` - the industry classification, explained on our SIC code lookup page.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Domicile is not location
Expect the two state fields to disagree. Rollins Inc is incorporated in Delaware but operates from Georgia. Global Medical Response, Inc. is a Delaware entity with a Colorado business address. If a report needs "where the company is," decide explicitly which of the two you mean before you build the column.

## Reverse CIK Lookup: Number to Company Name and State
### Confirming you have the right entity
A reverse lookup that returns a plausible-looking name is not the same as a confirmed match. Before you rely on it, check three things: that the filing history contains the forms you would expect for the entity type, that the business address is consistent with what you know about the company, and that the ticker array either matches your expectation or is legitimately empty. If any of the three surprises you, you may be looking at a subsidiary, a similarly named registrant, or a dormant shell. Recording the entity name next to every CIK you store makes this kind of mismatch visible later instead of silently propagating through a dataset.

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
**`cik-lookup-data.txt` is the full EDGAR CIK list** - every filer name the SEC has ever indexed, mapped to a CIK, in one plain-text file at `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt`. Where the ticker map covers listed companies only, this file covers individuals, funds, trusts, agents, dissolved registrants and historical names, which makes it the right source for an **EDGAR CIK database download**.

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
### Format and parsing
Each line is an uppercase filer name, then a colon, then the padded CIK, then a trailing colon. Names may themselves contain colons and commas, so split from the right, never from the left.
```  
import urllib.request

req = urllib.request.Request(  
    "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt",  
    headers={"User-Agent": "YourCompany you@example.com"})

index = {}  
for raw in urllib.request.urlopen(req):  
    line = raw.decode("latin-1").strip().rstrip(":")  
    if not line:  
        continue  
    name, _, cik = line.rpartition(":")  
    if cik.isdigit():  
        index.setdefault(name, cik)

print(len(index), "names indexed")  
```

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
### Practical notes before you rely on it
*   The file is large - stream it rather than reading it into memory as one string.  
*   Encoding is not clean UTF-8; decode with a permissive codec such as latin-1.  
*   Names are uppercase, so normalize your query the same way.  
*   One CIK can appear under several names, including former names.  
*   Refresh periodically; new registrants are added continuously.

## The cik-lookup-data.txt Bulk EDGAR CIK List
### When to use this instead of the tool above
Use the interactive lookup for one-off questions about listed companies. Use the bulk file when you need offline resolution, when you are matching thousands of names at once, or when your targets include non-listed entities such as private issuers and Section 16 individuals that the ticker map simply does not contain.

## EDGAR CIK Database Download Options Compared
**The SEC publishes several free bulk files that contain CIKs**, each with a different scope and shape. Choosing the right one first saves a great deal of parsing work later, so compare coverage before you write a downloader.

## EDGAR CIK Database Download Options Compared
### Index files are CIK-keyed too
Every quarterly and daily index row includes the CIK, the company name, the form type, the filing date and the document path. That makes the index files a second route to a name-to-CIK table, and the only convenient route to "every filer that submitted a given form in a given quarter."

## EDGAR CIK Database Download Options Compared
### Etiquette when downloading in bulk
*   Send a descriptive User-Agent containing a real contact address.  
*   Stay within the published fair-access limit of about 10 requests per second.  
*   Prefer one bulk file over thousands of individual requests.  
*   Cache aggressively and honor HTTP caching headers.  
*   Retry with backoff rather than hammering after an error.
The same etiquette applies to every endpoint discussed in our EDGAR API guide; sustained abuse gets IP addresses throttled.

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
**The submissions endpoint turns a CIK into a complete filing history** in one request: `https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json`, with the CIK padded to ten digits. It is the workhorse of EDGAR automation and returns both the entity's descriptive record and its recent filings as parallel arrays.

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### What the response contains
*   `cik`, `name`, `tickers`, `exchanges`, `entityType`.  
*   `sic`, `sicDescription`, `stateOfIncorporation`, `addresses`.  
*   `formerNames` with effective date ranges.  
*   `filings.recent` - parallel arrays of accession numbers, form types, filing dates and document names.  
*   `filings.files` - references to older pages of history for prolific filers.

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### A runnable example
```  
import json, urllib.request

def submissions(cik):  
    url = f"https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{str(cik).zfill(10)}.json"  
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={  
        "User-Agent": "YourCompany you@example.com"})  
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))

d = submissions(84839)  
print(d["name"], d["stateOfIncorporation"], d["addresses"]["business"]["stateOrCountry"])

rec = d["filings"]["recent"]  
for form, date, acc in list(zip(rec["form"], rec["filingDate"], rec["accessionNumber"]))[:5]:  
    print(form, date, acc)  
```

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### Building a document URL from the result
Filing documents live under `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accession-no-dashes}/{document}`. Note the inconsistency that trips people up: the path uses the _unpadded_ CIK while the JSON you just fetched used the padded one. Strip the dashes from the accession number for the folder name and keep them for display.

## Using a CIK in the EDGAR Submissions API
### Paging through a long filing history
The `filings.recent` block holds only the most recent tranche of submissions. Prolific filers - large banks, fund complexes, and any issuer with decades of ownership forms - overflow it, and the remainder is referenced in `filings.files` as additional JSON documents under the same submissions path. If you need a complete history you must fetch those extra files and concatenate them; skipping this step produces a truncated record that looks complete. A useful sanity check is to compare the earliest filing date you retrieved against the entity's known vintage, since a company with a five-digit CIK showing only three years of history is a clear sign that paging was missed.

## Using a CIK in EDGAR Full-Text Search
**Full-text search accepts a CIK as a filter**, which lets you search words inside one company's filings rather than across all of EDGAR. The system indexes filing documents from 2001 onward, so it complements - rather than replaces - the metadata search you get from the submissions API.
One Number Opens Five Doors

## Using a CIK in EDGAR Full-Text Search
### The query endpoint
The public interface is at `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=`, and the browser UI at `https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/` is built on it. Combine a quoted phrase with an entity restriction and, optionally, form and date filters. Our full-text search tool exposes the same filters without the URL assembly.

## Why Do You Need a CIK Number?
### For Analysts & Researchers
*   **Historical research** - track filings through renamings/mergers  
*   **Data normalization** - link SEC data to other databases  
*   **Filing tracking** - monitor a specific entity over time  
*   **Compliance** - verify which entity actually files with SEC  
*   **Cross-references** - match SEC data to CRSP or Compustat

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What is a CIK number?
A CIK (Central Index Key) is the unique identifier the SEC assigns to every entity that files with EDGAR. It is written as up to 10 digits, zero-padded on the left in its canonical form. Apple Inc.'s CIK is 0000320193 and MICROSOFT CORP's is 0000789019. A CIK never changes, even when the company renames itself or changes its ticker symbol.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What does CIK stand for in EDGAR?
CIK stands for Central Index Key. It is the number the SEC's systems use to identify corporations and individuals who have filed disclosure documents with the Commission. The same number is used across every SEC program area, so one CIK covers annual reports, ownership forms and institutional holdings reports alike.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Is an EDGAR CIK always 10 digits?
The canonical form is 10 digits with leading zeros, but the underlying number can be shorter. Apple's CIK is 320193 as an integer and 0000320193 when padded. Path-based endpoints such as data.sec.gov/submissions/ require the padded form, while query-string parameters like browse-edgar's CIK= accept either.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I look up a company by CIK number?
Pad the number to 10 digits and open https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000084839.json, substituting your CIK. The response gives the registrant's current name, former names, state of incorporation, business address, SIC code and complete filing history. For a rendered page instead, open https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?cik=84839.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I find a company's CIK from its ticker?
Use the lookup tool at the top of this page, which searches the SEC's official company_tickers.json file. For automated work, download that file once from https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json, build a ticker-to-CIK dictionary in memory, and resolve your whole list locally rather than issuing one request per ticker.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### How do I get a CIK number for my own company?
A CIK is issued automatically when an entity applies for EDGAR filing access through the SEC's filer-management process; you cannot request a specific number. The application also produces the private credentials used to transmit filings. Under EDGAR Next, access is managed through individual account credentials and authorized users, but the CIK itself is unchanged.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What is the difference between a CIK and a CIK confirmation code?
The CIK is public - it is printed on filings and published in SEC bulk files. The CIK Confirmation Code (CCC) is a private credential that pairs with the CIK to authorize a submission, as is the filer passphrase. Sharing a CIK is harmless; sharing a CCC or passphrase is not. EDGARScout never asks for filer credentials.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Why does one company have several CIK numbers?
Because EDGAR assigns CIKs to legal filing entities, not to brands. A group can have separate CIKs for the listed parent, financing subsidiaries and co-registrants, securitization trusts, registered fund trusts, and the advisory entity that files 13F reports. Choose the CIK by the form you need rather than by the most familiar name.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Does a CIK change when a company changes its name or ticker?
No. NAUTILUS, INC. became BOWFLEX INC. and kept CIK 0001078207; Facebook Inc became Meta Platforms, Inc. under 0001326801. EDGAR updates the name field and records the prior name in the formerNames array while the CIK stays fixed. A genuinely new legal registrant created by a merger does receive its own new CIK.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Can I look up a fund's CIK number?
Yes. Registered funds, ETFs, closed-end funds and the managers that file 13F reports all have CIKs. Search the registered legal name rather than the marketing name, and expect a layered structure: a registrant CIK for the trust, with S000 series identifiers and C000 class identifiers underneath it for individual funds and share classes.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Do individual people have CIK numbers?
Yes. Officers, directors and large shareholders who file Section 16 ownership forms have their own CIKs - Elon Musk's is 0001494730. EDGAR stores personal names surname-first with no comma, as "Musk Elon", so search the surname alone. The most reliable route is to open any Form 4 for the issuer and read the reporting person's CIK from the header.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Where can I download the full EDGAR CIK list?
The SEC publishes cik-lookup-data.txt at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/cik-lookup-data.txt, containing every filer name ever indexed with its padded CIK. Lines are name, colon, CIK, colon - split from the right because names can contain colons. For listed companies only, company_tickers.json is smaller and easier to work with.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### Why does my CIK search return multiple companies?
EDGAR matches your text against every registrant name, and many names overlap - subsidiaries, funds, dissolved shells and unrelated companies can all contain the same word. Use the state column and SIC description to discriminate, then open the candidate and confirm its filing history contains the forms you would expect from the entity you want.

## Frequently Asked Questions About CIK Number Lookup
### What happens to a CIK when a company is delisted or acquired?
Nothing is deleted. The CIK and the full filing archive remain permanently retrievable, and the history simply stops - often shortly after a Form 25 or Form 15. Because the current ticker map contains only survivors, any historical study must enumerate these dormant CIKs as well, or it will suffer from survivorship bias.
